newsitem.title: UK: Commodity fund approves aid for African cotton.
newsitem.headline: Commodity fund approves aid for African cotton.

text.p: The Common Fund for Commodities, (CFC), a U.N. organization, has approved a $3.6 million grant and a $5.7 million loan for improving cotton marketing and trade in Eastern and Southern Africa.
A CFC press release said the project activities will be piloted in Uganda and Tanzania, with provisions for dissemination of project results in the other cotton producing countries in the region.
The project will increase the benefits from cotton production and marketing through the establishment of a transparent and efficient market system within the framework of liberalization.
It will promote better access to the international market and introduce measures to minimise the exposure to technical and price risks.
The CFC said the project will develop and test a market system that responds to producer and trader needs and strengthen the public and private institutions to operate the system.
This will include a privately run warehousing system, a collateralizable warehouse receipt system, improved flow of information, quality assurance and certification.
The main beneficiaries of the project will be the farmers, traders, processors, financial institutions and governments of the participating countries, the CFC said.
